claim: A wah's manual byte moves its band-pass up the spectrum at every setting asked from 32: on 04 04 with the type's own modulator stilled, the band the profile peaks in climbs from 384 Hz at 32 to 3437 Hz at 127, on a line straight in octaves to within 0.077 at the four settings read, 0.0333 octaves a step. With the modulator running the same byte read 0.29 to 1.04 octaves higher at every setting and bent away from that line, so the bend round one read was the sweep's. Of the other rows read for this kind, the noise low-pass moves a hum that stands under the stimulus in a few bottom bands, two phasers were read with their own modulator running and the second wah through an overdrive. No law is set for a corner, and none is carried to another type.

measurements.why: 04 04's wah manual at five settings, every take's profile, and the depth its own modulator was left at.
04 02's wah manual, refused: the OD Sw it was walked at and each take's largest deviation.
01 73's hum low-pass at five settings with the hum raised, every take's profile.
04 06's phaser manual at two settings with the phaser mixed in and its own modulator running.
05 00's phaser manual at two settings, read with the type's phaser modulator running.
04 04's wah manual at four settings with the wah depth written to nothing, every take's profile, and the two bytes that say the filter stood still at the resonance the swept walk held.
The standing walk's own takes read a twelfth of an octave at a time, every take's profile, and the depth that held the filter still.

adds: The records give each take's level in each third-octave band. What is read out of them here is where the profile peaks, in octaves between bands, that on the one type admitted it climbs with the byte and bends, and which records cannot say where a corner is and why. The records name no filter, no centre and no table.

readings.at_the_bottom: At 0 the profile has two maxima of nearly one height and the takes land on either: 254, 600, 252 Hz. It is reported and not read as a location.

01 73.why: The hum raised to the top of its range and read under a held noise: the byte lifts a few bottom bands and has stopped moving by the last setting asked below the top two, and a hum is lines under a noise rather than a spectrum a corner can be located in.

04 06.why: A phaser's manual, read with the phaser mixed in and its own modulator running, like 05 00's; reported and neither a test nor a part of anything above.

05 00.why: A phaser's manual prints a different table from a wah's and was read at two settings with its own modulator running; reported, and neither a test nor a part of anything above.

readings.why: Locations are read per take and off the median profile of each setting's three takes, on the record's own band set.

refused.why: 04 02's wah manual walked with the type's overdrive on (OD Sw 40 03 0D at 01). A saturating stage after the filter spreads a band's energy into others, and a location read off the band set is read through it; refused before any location was read, by the same rule that refuses it for the resonance byte.

alternatives.reading: The time-averaged centre is straight in octaves over the byte.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: Through the readings at 32 and 127, a straight line in octaves misses 55 by -0.34, 95 by +0.33 octaves, against takes that agree to 0.084. Whether the bend is the byte's or the sweep's is what would take this claim off the shelf.

alternatives.reading: The bend read with the modulator running belongs to the byte.
alternatives.ruled_out_by: The sweep's. Swept, the peak sat under the line through its ends at 55 and over it at 95, by 0.34 and 0.33 octaves. Standing still it sits under at both, by 0.11 and 0.21, and the reading at 95 moved 0.54 octaves across the line, more than three half-bands.

alternatives.reading: The centre standing still is straight in octaves over the byte.
alternatives.taken_up_by: Straight. Read four times finer, the straight line that misses least misses every setting by 0.077 octaves, inside the one twelfth-octave band (0.083) the queue set for a straight centre before the read and short of the 0.104 a steepening one needed. The line through the two ends climbs 0.0333 octaves a step.

refuted_by: 04 04's manual walked with its modulator stilled at a setting between two asked here, putting the peak below the lower of them or more than a twelfth-octave band off the line through them.

the_round_that_stood_the_filter_still.what_was_asked: Whether the bend round one read in the centre belongs to the byte or to the modulator that swept the filter through every take: 04 04's wah manual at 32, 55, 95, 127 with the type's own wah depth (40 03 07) written to nothing, so the filter stands where the byte puts it.

the_queue_entry_it_answers.observable: 04 04's wah manual at 32, 55, 95, 127 with the type's own wah depth (40 03 07) written to nothing, so the filter stands where the byte puts it.
the_queue_entry_it_answers.sensitivity_here: How far the three takes of one setting put the peak apart in this record, 0.084 octaves at the widest from 32 up.

the_round_that_stood_the_filter_still.the_reading: Unchanged from round one: the band the median profile of each setting's three takes peaks in, moved by a parabola through it and its two neighbours, on the record's own third-octave band set, and the same per take.
the_round_that_stood_the_filter_still.against_the_predictions: Both were for 55: 1151 Hz at 55 if the centre is straight in octaves and 908 Hz at 55 if the bend is the byte's. Standing still the peak is at 622 Hz, 0.89 and 0.55 octaves under them, against takes that agree to 0.004 and against half a band, 0.167, which is as far as a reading held in one band can be off. Neither holds. Both were read off the swept walk's own ends, and the modulator did not only bend the reading: it lifted it, by 0.29 to 1.04 octaves at every setting asked.
the_round_that_stood_the_filter_still.what_the_bend_was: The sweep's. Swept, the peak sat under the line through its ends at 55 and over it at 95, by 0.34 and 0.33 octaves. Standing still it sits under at both, by 0.11 and 0.21, and the reading at 95 moved 0.54 octaves across the line, more than three half-bands.
the_round_that_stood_the_filter_still.why_straightness_is_not_decided: The standing centre climbs 0.0293, 0.0316 and 0.0405 octaves a step from the bottom up, and misses the line through its ends by up to 0.21 octaves against takes that agree to 0.016. That spread is not how well the peak is placed. At 32 and 55 the peak band stands more than five decibels over both neighbours, so the parabola hardly moves it off the band's centre and three takes agree because one band holds the peak each time. The reading is then good to half a band, 0.167 octaves, and the straight line that misses least misses every setting by at most 0.104. Whether the steepening is the byte's or where the band set puts a narrow peak is left open and queued.
the_round_that_stood_the_filter_still.why_it_is_no_longer_parked: It was parked because no row of this kind had been read standing still. One now has, and it was in a position to put the peak lower as the byte rose and did not.
the_round_that_stood_the_filter_still.what_it_does_not_close: A law in the byte. The standing centre is read at four settings on a band set a third of an octave wide, and nothing here names a table, a curve or a corner.

the_round_that_read_the_standing_walk_in.what_was_asked: The takes of the standing walk read again at a twelfth of an octave, with the same peak reading: whether the four positions still miss every straight line by more than the band set now resolves.

the_queue_entry_it_answers.observable: The takes of the standing walk read again at a twelfth of an octave, with the same peak reading: whether the four positions still miss every straight line by more than the band set now resolves.

predicts.straight: a line through all four within one twelfth-octave band, 0.083 octaves
predicts.steepening: no line within 0.104 octaves of all four, as on the third-octave set, the climb running 0.029 a step at the bottom and 0.041 at the top

the_queue_entry_it_answers.divergence: 0.104 octaves, the least any straight line misses the third-octave readings by.
the_queue_entry_it_answers.sensitivity_here: One twelfth-octave band, 0.083 octaves, the resolution this archive already queues and reads band positions at.

run.why: The takes are on disk, so it costs no time on the unit.

the_round_that_read_the_standing_walk_in.the_reading: Round one's, unchanged: the band the median profile peaks in, moved by a parabola through it and its two neighbours, on the finer record's own band set.
the_round_that_read_the_standing_walk_in.against_the_predictions: Straight. Read four times finer, the straight line that misses least misses every setting by 0.077 octaves, inside the one twelfth-octave band (0.083) the queue set for a straight centre before the read and short of the 0.104 a steepening one needed. The line through the two ends climbs 0.0333 octaves a step.
the_round_that_read_the_standing_walk_in.what_the_finer_set_did: It moved each reading by at most 0.094 octaves and it loosened the top: at 127 the peak band ties with a neighbour and the three takes land 0.11 octaves apart, against 0.016 on the coarser set. The finer read placed the narrow peaks at the bottom and scattered the broad one at the top.
the_round_that_read_the_standing_walk_in.what_it_does_not_close: Both settings between the ends still sit under the line through them, by 0.08 and 0.15 octaves, which is what a climb slightly steeper at the top would also give. The line that misses least spreads that lean to 0.077 over all four, inside one band, and the top setting's own takes scatter 0.11 apart, so the lean is reported and not read. The bar was met by 0.006 octaves, which is a thin margin and is said so. Four settings is also all the law is read at: nothing here says the byte has no step between them.
